payload.note: Source-filter separation decomposes a signal into source and filter parts; inverse-filtering is the primary method used: the speech signal is filtered with 1/H(z) where H(z) is the estimated vocal-tract transfer function to recover the excitation signal. Without the inverse-filtering algorithm, the separation technique cannot operate.

Source-filter separation decomposes a signal into source and filter parts; inverse-filtering is the primary method used: the speech signal is filtered with 1/H(z) where H(z) is the estimated vocal-tract transfer function to recover the excitation signal. Without the inverse-filtering algorithm, the separation technique cannot operate.

The vocal-tract entry is the human-made model of the vocal tract as an acoustic filter cavity in speech production theory. It is defined entirely in terms of its role as the filter component in the source-filter model: the model decomposes speech into source (glottal-flow) and filter (vocal-tract), and the vocal-tract construct cannot be separated from this framework.

In speech processing, inverse-filtering applies the reciprocal of the vocal-tract transfer function H(z) (estimated via linear prediction) to recover the glottal-flow excitation signal. The method depends on the vocal-tract being modeled as an all-pole filter, making the vocal-tract construct a structural prerequisite for the speech-context application of inverse-filtering.

Removing the source-filter model removes the conceptual framework that gives glottal-source its defined meaning.

Pinned sense (Law 11d): videolaryngoscopy is laryngoscopy performed with the laryngeal image displayed on a video monitor — 'a camera at the tip of the scope replaces the direct line of sight' (its accepted definition). High-speed-videolaryngoscopy is that examination with a high-speed camera integrated into the laryngoscope recording the vocal folds at 2000-10000 fps: the camera-tipped scope and the recorded image field are exactly videolaryngoscopy's carve, with the added frame-rate parameter. A competent speaker would call HSV 'a videolaryngoscopy' (a high-speed one); videolaryngoscopy is the nearest accepted kind, closer than laryngoscopy itself, whose direct-vision carve is replaced by the camera. [Law 9, 11]

Pinned sense (Law 11d): videolaryngoscopy is laryngoscopy performed with the laryngeal image displayed on a video monitor — 'a camera at the tip of the scope replaces the direct line of sight, so the image is recorded, transmitted, and shared' (its accepted definition). Stroboscopy is exactly that examination with one added parameter: a camera and laryngoscope capture the laryngeal image to a monitor, with the illumination modulated in brief pulses synchronized to the folds' fundamental frequency (its accepted definition names the Karl Storz and Richard Wolf camera-based systems as its instances). A competent speaker would call laryngeal stroboscopy a videolaryngoscopy (a strobe-illuminated one); the camera-tipped scope and monitor display are videolaryngoscopy's carve, and the strobe flash is the added parameter — as frame rate was for high-speed videolaryngoscopy. videolaryngoscopy is the nearest accepted kind, closer than laryngoscopy itself, whose direct-vision carve is replaced by the camera. [Law 9, 11]
